compiled_state.title: As a DSO operator, the deploy cutover for the new sub-PR workflow + required-checks + ledger keying does not brick in-flight PRs
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Provide a coordinated cutover that handles (1) v1.1.0 cycle_ledger entries that pre-date S2's re-keying, (2) in-flight sub-PRs that pre-date S1's workflow deploy, (3) `.github/required-checks.txt` manifest updates for S1's new `review-sub-pr` check-context and S4's RED-test-blocker check-context, (4) GitHub Ruleset updates for branch protection on `main` and `session-*` patterns, and (5) a one-shot script that marks in-flight open PRs as exempt from the newly-required checks for one grace window.

**Why**: When S1's workflow is deployed, sub-PRs already open will not have been reviewed by it (the workflow only triggers on new pushes). When S2's re-keying lands, defenses stored under the old sha-only key may be silently dropped. When S4's required check is added to branch protection, every in-flight PR becomes unmergeable until it re-runs CI. Without a coordinated migration, the cutover bricks the merge pipeline for every open PR.

**Scope**:
- IN: Migration script for v1.1.0 → v1.2.0 ledger entries (uses S2's sentinel-pr_number rule); `.github/required-checks.txt` manifest update; GitHub Ruleset update via `gh api` or equivalent; one-shot script marking in-flight PRs as exempt for one grace window (the exemption is logged); `validate-required-checks.sh` and `check-ruleset-preflight.sh` run against the new manifest; rollback script that reverts the workflow + ledger if cutover fails; cutover window documented in `CI-INTEGRATION.md`.
- OUT: The S1 workflow itself; the S2 keying change; the S4 required-check registration.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a migration script (`plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-ledger-v11-to-v12.sh` or equivalent) walks all existing PR comment markers and either re-keys v1.1.0 entries via the sentinel-pr_number rule or marks them as legacy-read-only.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #2 (migration for in-flight PRs and existing v1.1.0 entries)

- When this story is complete, `.github/required-checks.txt` is updated to include S1's new `review-sub-pr` check-context name AND S4's RED-test-blocker check-context name (under the umbrella job name). `validate-required-checks.sh` passes against the new manifest.
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #5 (required-checks manifest update)

- When this story is complete, GitHub Ruleset / branch protection on `main` is updated to require the new check-contexts. The update is staged: first the new check is added as NON-REQUIRED (informational), then promoted to required AFTER a one-week observation window in which the check is observed to pass on representative PRs.
  ← Satisfies: Scenario mitigation (required-check rollout)

- When this story is complete, a one-shot script (`plugins/dso/scripts/exempt-in-flight-prs.sh`) lists currently-open PRs and applies a documented exemption (e.g., a `migration-grace` label) so they can merge without re-running CI for the new check. The exemption is logged in `.tickets-tracker/migration-exemptions.json` or similar.  <!-- tickets-boundary-ok: documentation example illustrating exemption logging path -->
  ← Satisfies: Red team Finding #5 (in-flight PR exemption)

- When this story is complete, a rollback script (`plugins/dso/scripts/rollback-sub-pr-cutover.sh`) reverts the workflow + ledger + branch protection if cutover fails. The rollback is tested in a sandbox.
  ← Satisfies: Migration safety (cutover reversibility)

- When this story is complete, the cutover window and rollback procedure are documented in `plugins/dso/docs/CI-INTEGRATION.md` (doc-story consumes this).
  ← Satisfies: Migration safety (documentation)

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic (migration script, exemption script, rollback script).
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done requirement

## Considerations

- [Reliability] The migration script MUST be idempotent — re-running it must not corrupt entries that were already migrated.
- [Reliability] The rollback script MUST be runnable WITHOUT depending on the new workflow or new ledger format being intact.
- [Sequencing] Run this story AFTER S1, S2, S4 have all landed. Running it earlier (e.g., between S1 landing and S2 landing) creates an intermediate state where the manifest references a new check but the ledger is still v1.1.0.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

S_migration IMPLEMENTATION PLAN COMPLETE.

**Approach**: P1 — 5 focused single-purpose scripts (one per artifact). Matches existing migrate-*.sh codebase precedent (migrate-story-pr-bases.sh, migrate-dso-workflow-config.sh, migrate-review-defenses.sh). Score P1=24/25 vs P2 mega-orchestrator 13/25 (premature abstraction) vs P3 hybrid+checkpoint 17/25 (YAGNI on resumability).

**Tasks (10)**:
- T1+T2 ledger migration (depends on S2.T2 cross-story)
- T3+T4 required-checks manifest (depends on S1.T3 + S4.T4 cross-story)
- T5 ruleset staged rollout
- T6+T7 exempt-in-flight-prs (operational log at docs/migration-exemptions/ NOT in event-sourced tracker)
- T8+T9 rollback (independent of post-migration state)
- T10 cutover runbook doc
